papers.summary: DisMUSE develops distributed Muon-style spectral optimization with Newton-Schulz and low-rank momentum communication, directly targeting convergence and communication-quality tradeoffs.
papers.relevance: Strong match for spectral optimization, Newton-Schulz methods, low-rank communication, and training-efficiency tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: rank-32 compression reduces the simulated communication payload by 40.5%, from 385.39 to 229.34 GB.
NS achieves comparable accuracy to SVD (89.92% versus 89.69%) while reducing mean training time from 98.61 to 48.88 minutes.

papers.title: DisMUSE: An Efficient Distributed Singular-Spectrum-Based Optimization Approach with Theoretical Convergence Guarantee

papers.summary: Analyzes how finite Newton-Schulz depth changes rank selection and enables matrix-factorization trajectories to bypass early saddles.
papers.relevance: Directly relevant to Muon dynamics, rank selection, and spectral optimization theory.

evidence.quote: the number of Newton-Schulz steps can change the rank selected during the early stages of training

papers.title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle

papers.summary: ResQAdam combines low-rank optimizer-state updates with residual sign information for memory-efficient quantization-aware LLM training.
papers.relevance: Strong match for optimizer-state compression, memory-efficient training, throughput, and quality tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: It reduces optimizer-state memory by 71% to 74% relative to AdamW
lowers training throughput by less than 2%

papers.title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training

papers.summary: GEAR uses tangent-normal geometry and spectral information to evolve LoRA rank according to task-relevant directions.
papers.relevance: Strong match for dynamic rank allocation, LoRA geometry, and spectral adaptation.

evidence.quote: the leading normal singular directions yield the locally optimal rank expansion

papers.title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA

papers.summary: Studies singular-spectrum and subspace dynamics of LoRA in supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, attributing differences partly to baseline subtraction.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses how optimization regimes affect LoRA spectra and subspaces.

evidence.quote: Tracking the singular spectrum and subspaces of LoRA updates

papers.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning

papers.summary: BiMuon introduces geometry-aware stochastic bilevel optimization with Muon-style matrix updates and analyzes spectral imbalance.
papers.relevance: Relevant to matrix optimization, Muon updates, curvature, and convergence theory.

evidence.quote: the lower-level (LL) problem curvature can induce significant spectral imbalance in the upper-level (UL) geometry

papers.title: BiMuon: A Geometry-Aware Stochastic Bilevel Optimization Approach

papers.summary: Studies how learning rules, weight decay, and optimizer choices steer memorization-to-generalization behavior and effective circuit size.
papers.relevance: Strong match for generalization, memorization, regularization, compressibility, and optimizer effects.

evidence.quote: Learning rule choice thus steers circuit size, trading robustness against compressibility and transfer speed

papers.title: Grokking Can Be Steered: Selecting Desirable Solutions By Choice Of Learning Rule

papers.summary: SaMA proposes a Kronecker-based PEFT parameterization whose effective rank scales more favorably with parameter budget and whose geometry is more optimizer-friendly.
papers.relevance: Relevant to low-rank parameterizations, PEFT, rank scaling, and optimization geometry.

evidence.quote: its invariance manifold induces flat directions in the loss landscape, creating an optimization bottleneck for adaptive optimizers

papers.title: SaMA: Morpho Adaptation via Asymmetric Expansion of Kronecker Product

papers.summary: Presents a forward-only method for selecting SVD components to reduce LLM weight rank with lower memory and greater speed than gradient-based search.
papers.relevance: Directly relevant to singular-value-based compression, model adaptation, memory, and speed.

evidence.quote: our forward-only search then efficiently identifies the weight matrix with the highest dispersion that merits rank reduction

papers.title: Efficient LLM Adaptation with Forward-Only Passes

papers.summary: SCALAR performs PEFT by learning scalar coefficients over fixed task-calibrated directions, reducing trainable state and training memory.
papers.relevance: Strong match for memory-efficient fine-tuning and quality-throughput tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: SCALAR achieves performance comparable to LoRA with substantially fewer trainable parameters, lower peak training memory, and higher throughput.
20% lower peak training memory and 6% higher throughput than LoRA

papers.title: Direction or Magnitude? Learning Scalars over Task-Calibrated Directions

papers.summary: Defines behavioral rate as the compressed adapter size needed to preserve fine-tuning behavior and studies how it depends on data, receiver model, and noise.
papers.relevance: Especially relevant to low-rank compressibility, adapter information, singular directions, and corrupted training data.

evidence.quote: fine-tuning compressibility is a property of the dataset--receiver pair rather than of the dataset alone

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: Examines delayed effects of temporary weight decay in Muon-trained Transformers across several model scales.
papers.relevance: Directly relevant to spectral/weight regularization, Muon optimization, and scale-dependent training behavior.

evidence.quote: temporary weight decay in Muon-trained decoder-only Transformers

papers.title: Delayed Effects of Temporary Weight Decay in Muon Pretraining

papers.summary: DictLLM performs post-training LLM compression using shared SVD dictionaries, sparse coefficients, and factor-specific quantization.
papers.relevance: Strong match for low-rank compressibility, singular spectra, quantization, and memory-quality tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: Post-training compression is an effective approach to managing this trade-off

papers.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels

papers.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of Muon for Transformer next-token prediction, including spectral margins, convergence, weight structure, and generalization.
papers.relevance: Relevant to theoretical understanding of Muon, spectral structure, and LLM optimization.

evidence.quote: we characterize the optimization trajectory exactly and show that the normalized spectral margin is optimal after each update

papers.title: Theoretical Analysis of Muon on Transformers for Next-Token Prediction

papers.summary: LIRA allocates LoRA rank dynamically using interpretable second-order loss-trajectory signals under matched parameter budgets.
papers.relevance: Directly relevant to optimization-aware rank allocation and interpretable LoRA behavior.

evidence.quote: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation
